answer: Agents resist sybil floods by forcing costly progressive bonding before any voting power unlocks. At dawn of an account lifecycle, the network admits only observers; to forge a second persona you must lock capital and wait through timed cooling periods that scale with claimed influence. Peer graders mark suspicious clusters with a violet risk flag when many identities share timing patterns or funding trails. Cheap clones never clear those gates, so manufactured majorities stay uneconomic while real workers keep earning attestations.
